A 30-day visa-exempt stay can be extended once, by up to 30 days, at Koh Samui Immigration, 333 Maenam Road, Soi 1, Maenam. You fill in form TM.7 and pay 1,900 THB in cash, and approval is at the officer's discretion. Bring your passport with signed copies, one 4×6 cm photo, proof of your Samui address (the TM.30 receipt if you rent privately) and ideally an onward flight.

Last checked: November 2026. Since 15 September 2026, visitors from the 60 visa-exempt countries get 30 days on arrival, not 60. If you arrived on or before 14 September 2026, your original stamp still applies. Rules can change without notice, so call the office on +66 77 423 440 before you go.

Who can extend, and for how long

Most short-stay entries can be extended once in Thailand. The table shows the usual outcome at a provincial office such as Samui.

How you enteredExtension on SamuiFee
Visa exemption, 30 days (60 countries)Once, up to 30 days1,900 THB
Visa exemption, 15 days (Mauritius, Seychelles)Ask the office; discretionary1,900 THB
Tourist visa (TR), 60 daysOnce, up to 30 days1,900 THB
Destination Thailand Visa (DTV), 180-day entryOnce per entry, up to 180 days1,900 THB

Visa on arrival (Azerbaijan, Belarus, Serbia)Short extensions only in exceptional cases1,900 THB
Entered on or before 14 Sep 2026 with a 60-day stampOnce, up to 30 days, as before1,900 THB

A visa-on-arrival extension is normally granted only for illness or similar emergencies. [check]

You can't extend a visa exemption twice in a row on Samui. After the 30-day extension, you must leave Thailand or switch to the right long-stay visa from abroad. Our Thailand visa guide covers every option, including the DTV.

DTV extensions on Samui

Destination Thailand Visa holders get up to 180 days per entry and can extend each entry once by up to 180 days, for 1,900 THB, at Koh Samui Immigration. Bring the same basics as a tourist (passport, copies, photo, TM.7, TM.30 receipt) plus evidence that you still meet the visa's purpose: a remote-work contract or client invoices for the "workcation" route, or a current enrolment letter for a Muay Thai or cooking course. Officers can also ask to see recent bank statements. If you stay longer than 90 days in a row, you must also file a 90-day report (TM.47). Our digital nomad guide to Koh Samui covers the DTV in depth.

Families and children

Each family member needs their own TM.7, photo, copies and 1,900 THB fee, babies included. Children usually have to attend with a parent. If one parent is applying for a child alone, bring a copy of the other parent's passport and be ready to explain the arrangement. Plan the visit for a weekday morning so the children aren't waiting through the heat of the afternoon. Our Koh Samui with kids guide has ideas for the rest of the day.

Documents checklist

Make all copies before you leave your hotel and sign each one. Missing paperwork is the most common reason people are sent away.

  • Your original passport.
  • Signed copies of the passport photo page, the page with your latest entry stamp, and any previous extension or visa page.
  • A copy of your TDAC confirmation (the officer may ask for it).
  • Form TM.7, filled in with a blue or black pen. Blank forms are at the office and on the Immigration Bureau website.
  • One recent 4×6 cm colour photo, taken within the last 6 months.
  • 1,900 THB in cash. Bring the exact amount; counters may not have change.
  • Proof of address on Samui: hotel booking confirmation, or a rental contract plus the landlord's TM.30 receipt.
  • An onward or return flight out of Thailand, in case it is requested.

Hotels file the TM.30 address notification automatically. If you rent a private villa or condo, ask your landlord for the TM.30 receipt a few days before your appointment. Immigration usually asks for it.

  • Bank letters or proof of funds are not normally needed for a tourist extension, but carry a recent statement on your phone.
  • Photos printed on plain paper or taken more than 6 months ago are often refused.

Step by step at the office

  1. Before Check that your stamp ends within about 7–10 days. Applying earlier is fine, because the new 30 days are added to the end of your current permission, but you gain nothing by going weeks ahead.
  2. 08:00 Arrive before the doors open at 08:30. Queues build fast in high season (December–April) and on Mondays.
  3. 08:30 Present your documents for an initial check and take a queue number.
  4. Wait When your number is called, hand over the TM.7, photo, copies and passport, and pay the 1,900 THB. Keep the receipt.
  5. Collect Wait for your passport with the new extension stamp. Check the date before you leave the counter.

Expect anything from 1 to 3 hours. The Immigration Bureau's online appointment system lists a calendar for "Suratthani Immigration (Samui)", so look for a slot before you go. [check]

Dress and behaviour

Dress as you would for a bank: long trousers or a knee-length skirt, a shirt or top that covers your shoulders, and closed shoes or neat sandals. Shorts, vests and beachwear can get you sent away. Keep calm and polite, even if the queue is slow. Officers have discretion, and a respectful applicant has the best chance.

Copies and photos

Don't count on a photocopier or photo booth at the office. Copy shops and photo studios in Maenam, Bophut and Chaweng do passport copies for a few baht a page and 4×6 cm photos in minutes. Many hotels will print copies at reception.

When to go

Tuesday to Thursday mornings are usually the quietest. Mondays and the first working day after a long Thai holiday are the busiest. In the November rains, allow extra time on the ring road and carry your documents in a waterproof bag; see the Koh Samui weather guide. If you are staying on Koh Phangan or Koh Tao, Samui is not your office: those islands have their own immigration services, and rough seas from October to December can cancel ferries.

There is parking for scooters and cars. Grab works on the north coast, and songthaews run along the ring road, but a return taxi or a rented scooter is simpler. Only ride if you hold a licence with the motorcycle category and wear a helmet: police checkpoints on the ring road fine riders up to 2,000 THB for no helmet. See getting around Koh Samui, motorbike rental on Koh Samui and our Maenam area guide.

Costs

  • Government fee: 1,900 THB per person, paid in cash at the counter. Children pay the same fee.
  • Copies and photos: roughly 100–200 THB in total.
  • Transport: a taxi from Chaweng and back costs more than the fee itself in some cases; a scooter costs a few hundred baht for the day.
  • Visa agents: agencies in Chaweng, Lamai and Bophut charge a service fee on top of the 1,900 THB to prepare paperwork and accompany you. Fees vary widely, so ask for a written price.

Don't expect to pay the fee by card. Withdraw cash before you go; there are bank ATMs and 7-Elevens along the ring road through Maenam, but foreign-card ATMs charge 220–250 THB per withdrawal, so take out enough in one go. See banks and ATMs on Koh Samui.

Whatever an agent promises, the extension is still decided by the immigration officer, and you must attend in person.

If your extension is refused

Refusals are rare for first-time tourist extensions with complete documents, but they happen, especially to people with many back-to-back entries. If you are refused:

  • Leave Thailand on or before the last day of your current stamp. That date doesn't change.
  • Don't overstay. The fine is 500 THB per day, capped at 20,000 THB, and overstays of more than 90 days bring a re-entry ban.
  • Fly out (Samui has direct flights to Singapore, and Bangkok has flights everywhere) and return with the right visa, or apply for a tourist visa or DTV from abroad.

If a storm cancels your ferry or flight on your last day, keep the cancellation notice and report to immigration at once. Officers deal with weather delays every monsoon season.

Using a visa agent

Legitimate agents fill in forms, check your documents, book your slot and come with you to Maenam. That can be worth it if you have a complicated case, such as a DTV extension or a marriage visa.

Avoid anyone who offers a "stamp service", "border bounce without leaving", or an extension without you attending. These are illegal, and fake stamps can lead to arrest, deportation and a ban. Never hand over your passport without a written receipt showing the agent's company name, the date and what they are doing with it. Our Koh Samui scams guide lists other traps, and the Tourist Police (1155) can help if an agent keeps your passport.

Signs of a trustworthy agent: a registered office address, a written quote, a receipt for every document, and honest answers about what they can't guarantee. Signs to walk away: "100% approval", requests for extra cash "for the officer", or pressure to pay before they have seen your passport stamps.

Plan your extra 30 days

An extension means more time for the islands. Pig Island runs all year: the Pig Island speedboat tour costs 1,450 THB per adult. The Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan day trip is 2,200 THB per adult. If your extension takes you past 16 December, Ang Thong National Marine Park will be open again (it closes from 1 November to 15 December). For a longer stay, compare monthly rentals on our Koh Samui villas page and read our long-stay guide. Residents with 90-day reports and re-entry permits should read our Koh Samui immigration office guide.
